dct_description_sm: This multi-year project aimed to improve the adaptive capacity of four Aboriginal communities along the northern coast of the St. Lawrence River in order to reduce risks associated with coastal erosion potentially increased by climate change. The overarching goal of the project was to assess the current vulnerabilities and project future vulnerabilities for these communities in response to climate change.   In the first year of this multiyear project, the objectives were as follows: (1) to map the different social, economic, cultural and traditional coastal activities on the Northern Coast of the St. Lawrence River; (2) to identify issues and concerns of the Aboriginal communities in the context of coastal geo-risks, climate change and adaptation strategies, (3) to analyze the unique perspective of coastal Aboriginal communities concerning coastal geo-risks and climate change impacts on their lifestyles; and (4) to evaluate the vulnerability of coastal communities to climate change impacts.  The second year concentrated on a quantitative study of risks and the development of mapping tools. Specific objectives were to: - create a preliminary map of different social, economic, cultural, and traditional activities in the coastal zone - characterize and map coastal occupation - identify possible coastal risks posed by climate change on Aboriginal communities - examine historical weather data and analyze coastal hazards - conduct a preliminary qualitative assessment on vulnerabilities related to infrastructure, coastal hazards, and climate change - analyze the perceptions of public actors and residents on coastal hazards and climate change.
